subject: gk
question: Which of the following is the function of trade barriers?

options.text: Restrict the flow of international goods and services
Restrict the flow of Indian goods and services in India

solution:
The correct answer is __**Restrict the flow of international goods and services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Trade barriers are measures implemented by governments to control the flow of goods and services across international borders, often to protect domestic industries.
 
• These barriers include tariffs (taxes on imports), quotas (limits on the number of goods that can be imported), and non-tariff barriers like licensing and standards.
 
• The primary purpose of trade barriers is to **restrict international competition** and encourage the growth of local industries by limiting the availability of foreign products.
 
• They can also be used to safeguard national security, protect jobs, or enforce trade sanctions against specific countries.
 
• While trade barriers can benefit domestic producers, they may also lead to higher prices for consumers and trade tensions between countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Trade Barriers:**

 
 
• **Tariffs:** Taxes imposed on imported goods to make them more expensive than domestic products.
 
• **Quotas:** Numerical limits on the quantity of goods that can be imported.
 
• **Subsidies:** Financial support provided to domestic industries to make them more competitive against foreign imports.
 
• **Non-tariff barriers:** Regulations or standards that make it harder for foreign goods to enter the market, such as health and safety standards.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Trade Barriers:**
 
 
• Positive: Protects local industries and jobs, encourages domestic production, and enhances national security.
 
• Negative: Increases prices for consumers, limits product variety, and can lead to retaliatory measures by other countries.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Trade Barriers:**
 
 
• The Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930 imposed high tariffs on imports into the U.S., worsening the global economic depression.
 
• The EU imposes quotas on certain agricultural products to protect its farmers.
 
 
 
• **Global Trade Organizations:**
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO):** Works to reduce trade barriers globally and resolve trade disputes between nations.
 
• **Regional Trade Agreements:** Examples include NAFTA (now USMCA) and the European Union, which aim to reduce barriers within specific regions.
 
 
 
• **Recent Trends:** Many countries are revisiting trade barriers to protect local industries amidst global economic shifts, as seen during the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing geopolitical tensions.
